beats.text: First night in a hotel. And you sleep terribly.
Researchers measured people's brains during their first night in a new place.
One half of the brain, the left, stayed more alert than the other.
It reacted more to strange sounds. And woke people up faster.
By the second night, the difference was gone.
It's called the first night effect. A built-in night watch.

sources: Tamaki, Bang, Watanabe & Sasaki (2016). Night watch in one brain hemisphere during sleep associated with the first-night effect in humans. Current Biology 26(9). 35 volunteers; left-hemisphere default-mode network more active in slow-wave sleep on night 1; deviant sounds to the right ear woke people more and faster; no asymmetry on night 2. Via Brown University news.
